solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Synthesised obscure alien enzyme

indicators.note: something synthesised is built up anew, so the letters of the next two words are put together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A lab report on an unfamiliar, foreign enzyme someone has made artificially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Synthesised' looks like a description of the enzyme but is the anagram signal for the twelve letters of OBSCURE ALIEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribonuclease is a biological catalyst that breaks down RNA, so it is a type of enzyme.

clue.text: Tester's torn, broken by time

indicators.note: a word broken by another has that other pushed into its middle, so the word for torn is split open

parts.note: a rent is a tear, something torn
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone who checks things finds their work ripped up by the passage of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Tester' means 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a reagent is a substance used to test for the presence of another, hence a tester.

clue.text: Open-plan residence adapted to big modernist

indicators.note: adapted means altered to suit, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An open-plan home has been converted for a famous modernist architect.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is TO BIG MODERNIST, fourteen letters, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed-sitting room is a single room serving as both bedroom and living space, a one-room open-plan lodging.

clue.text: One chap gets up, offering place for old woman

indicators.note: to offer a place for something is to make room for it inside, so the letter for old goes in
in a down clue, getting up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man stands up and gives his seat to an elderly lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets up' reverses I MAN to NAMI; 'offering place for' puts O inside. 'old woman' wants to be the definition, but 'old' gives the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female name, the mother-in-law of Ruth in the Bible, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: What can secure clip joint

parts.note: to clip someone is to cuff them, give a light blow
a link is a joint or connection

explanation.surface: Asking what might hold a club of ill repute, a clip joint, safely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clip joint' reads as one phrase, a club that overcharges, but splits into a blow and a connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A cufflink is a fastener that holds a shirt cuff closed, so something that can secure.

clue.text: Long in the picture

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning their junction

explanation.surface: Something is included in a photograph or a film for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'thE PICture'.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic as an adjective means extended and grand in scale, like a lengthy film or poem.

clue.text: Source book lacking over rugby player

parts.note: a spring is a source of water

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the letter for over is taken from the word book

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A reference book is missing, which overrides a rugby player.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing O from BOOK leaves BOK.
explanation.definitionFit: The Springboks are the South African national rugby team, so each member is a rugby player.

clue.text: Source of tunes Barnum perhaps used with tumblers?

parts.note: Barnum is a stage musical about the showman P T Barnum, so an example of a musical
tumblers are drinking glasses

explanation.surface: Asks if the great showman Barnum made music with acrobats, tumblers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumblers' suggests circus acrobats beside Barnum, but means drinking vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical glasses are a set of tuned wine glasses played by rubbing the rims, an instrument producing melodies.

clue.text: Like satay Queen's left on one side?

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letters for the Queen go out of the word

parts.note: satay is meat cooked on skewers, so it is skewered
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen; the 's means has

explanation.surface: Describing satay, the Queen has left some on the side of her plate.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ER from SKEWERED leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something skewed is lopsided, slanting to one side, askew.

clue.text: Sound of Monteverdi, perhaps, not 10CC?

indicators.note: not means without, so the letters for the measure are removed from the composer's name

parts.note: Claudio Monteverdi was the Italian composer; the forename is shared with others, hence perhaps
ten cubic centimetres make one centilitre, CL

explanation.surface: Is the music of Monteverdi not that of the 1970s band 10cc?
explanation.walkthrough: 10CC looks like the British pop group but is a volume, ten cubic centimetres, equal to one centilitre.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio means reproduced sound, as opposed to the visual part of a recording.

clue.text: Outlaw out of order?

parts.note: one of Robin Hood's band of outlaws was a monk outside his religious order, living in the forest

explanation.surface: A criminal behaving badly, or a machine that has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' reads as tidiness, but it is a religious order such as the Franciscans.
explanation.definitionFit: Friar Tuck is the jovial cleric among Robin Hood's merry men in Sherwood Forest.

clue.text: Desirable belle's wild about one soldier

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the other pieces
wild means unruly, so the letters of the word belle are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written; the 's means is
one is the Roman numeral I
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A desirable young beauty is crazy about a single soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns BELLE into ELBLE, and 'about' wraps it round IGI.
explanation.definitionFit: Eligible describes someone attractive as a marriage partner, a desirable catch.

clue.text: One novel — about six as one's aim

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for novel goes round the number

parts.note: novel means new
six is VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Reads like a reader's target of finishing a single novel in about six days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' wants to be a book, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something in view is to have it as a goal or intention.

clue.text: Test creator admitting to coaching

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the word to goes inside the name

parts.note: Alan Turing devised the Turing test for machine intelligence

explanation.surface: Whoever writes an exam confesses to giving private lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test creator' looks like an examiner but is Alan Turing, the British computing pioneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutoring is private teaching, the same as coaching a pupil.

clue.text: Concerned with new climb and gaining fresh energy

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A climber, worried about a new ascent, is getting a second wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means being reborn or revived, coming back into vigour.

clue.text: A poet penning round on a banker?

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the poet's word holds the round letter

parts.note: a bard is a poet
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A poet writes a round, a song, about a financier.
explanation.walkthrough: A banker is a fishing boat working the Newfoundland Banks, not a financier.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on a ship, and a banker is a type of fishing vessel.

clue.text: A masculine home counties boy gone up north?

definitions.text: A masculine home counties boy gone up north?

indicators.note: in a down clue, gone up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: SE, south-east, is where the home counties around London lie
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A man from the area around London has moved to northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone up' reverses AMSELAD to DALESMA. The home counties are the counties around London.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalesman lives in the Yorkshire Dales, in the north, so a southern lad who moved there would be one.

clue.text: Beginning putting out day's sunshade

indicators.note: putting out means ejecting, so the letter for day is thrown out of the word

parts.note: dawning means beginning
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: At dawn, someone sets up the day's sunshade.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing D from DAWNING leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas cover stretched over a shopfront or window to keep off sun.

clue.text: Damage following aircraftman's approach

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the word for damage goes after the airman

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for aircraftman, the lowest RAF rank
damage is informal for cost, as in what's the damage

explanation.surface: A wrecked plane follows an airman's line of approach.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and address them boldly.

clue.text: Period silver, English, in chests under diamonds

indicators.note: under means placed after in this across clue, so the chests follow the diamonds letter

parts.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: in means inside, so silver and English go within the chests

parts.note: arks are chests or coffers
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A treasure hoard: silver and English coins in chests beneath diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dark Ages are the early medieval era, a historical period.

clue.text: NE types roaming here in London?

indicators.note: roaming means wandering, so the letters of these words wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether people from the north-east wander here in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Stepney is a district in the East End of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepney is a place in east London, so it fits a location in the capital.

clue.text: Something like cardinal, perhaps, to advance on church

indicators.note: on means placed after in an across clue, so the word for advance follows the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to rise is to advance or go up

explanation.surface: A cardinal seeking promotion in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests the cleric but is the colour cardinal red.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerise is a deep cherry red, a shade close to cardinal red.

clue.text: Was head returning from conscious state?

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for was head is read backwards

parts.note: to have led is to have been at the head
aware means conscious

explanation.surface: Was someone's head coming back from consciousness?
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: Friend from that time protecting me

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the word for that time shields the note inside

parts.note: ago refers back to a time past
me, or mi, is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A friend who has been looking out for someone since long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for a friend, widely used informally in English.

clue.text: Shut up shop

definitions.meaning: to confine in a small space

explanation.definitionFit: Coop means to confine, and the Co-op is a British chain of cooperative stores.

clue.text: Bullfighter cuts a great deal, mostly where stock is kept

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so the bullfighter goes inside
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: some means to a great extent, as in he cried some
a torero is a bullfighter

explanation.surface: A matador slashes prices on a huge amount of the stock in a warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a great deal' reads as a bargain alongside 'cuts', but it is the informal American sense of 'some', to a great extent.
explanation.definitionFit: A storeroom is a room for keeping goods or supplies.

clue.text: Author of The Railway Children losing time over another writer

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the remaining letters are read backwards
losing means giving up, so the letter for time is removed

parts.note: E Nesbit wrote the children's novel The Railway Children

explanation.surface: A children's author runs out of time and gives way to another writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing T from NESBIT leaves NESBI; 'over' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was a Norwegian playwright, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Vastly upset and soundly troubled

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of these two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is greatly disturbed, then troubled even in their sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'troubled' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupendously means to an amazing degree, enormously.
